title: McQuillan's Bridge rehabilitation recommended
subtitle: Also: closed meeting investigator, community grants, procurement by-law, outside water use, energy equity and building permit fees.
overview: The committee recommended rehabilitating and strengthening the 110-year-old McQuillan's Bridge rather than replacing it {{vote:m10}}. Staff estimated the work at about $2.9 million with a 30-year design life before reassessment. The bridge is heritage designated, and councillors weighed preservation and trail connection against the higher cost of rehabilitation compared with a steel replacement.

The committee also recommended appointing Aird & Berlis LLP as the City's Closed Meeting Investigator {{vote:m2}}, and asked the City Clerk to review closed-meeting practices as part of the 2027 Governance Review {{vote:m3}}. It recommended an updated Community Investment Strategy {{vote:m7}}, a new Procurement By-law taking effect September 1, 2026 {{vote:m8}}, and a rewritten Outside Water Use By-law with two restriction levels {{vote:m11}}.

It further recommended receiving the Energy Equity Action Plan {{vote:m12}} and new building permit fees to restore cost recovery and rebuild the building reserve {{vote:m15}}. Staff will report on military reservist leave top-up {{vote:m9}}. After a closed session, the Mayor reported that Council gave staff direction on two items, but no details were released. All of these are recommendations that Council will consider later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the assessment and issuing a Notice of Completion to rehabilitate and strengthen the bridge, rather than replace it {{vote:m10}}.
The committee recommended appointing Aird & Berlis LLP as the City's Closed Meeting Investigator and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign the agreement.
The committee directed the City Clerk to review closed-meeting protocols, the Procedure By-law and best practices to increase transparency and reporting in the 2027 Governance Review.
The committee recommended approving the updated strategy, with new grant streams and inflationary adjustments subject to future budget updates.
The committee recommended approving an updated Procurement By-law taking effect September 1, 2026.
The committee recommended a new by-law replacing the 2014 one, with standard and elevated restriction levels.
The committee received the plan and directed staff to determine resourcing and financial impacts through the multi-year budget process.
The committee recommended new fee schedules, a higher reserve target range, automatic indexing from 2028, and a review of new administrative fees for the 2027 budget.

debate: On McQuillan's Bridge, supporters of rehabilitation pointed to its heritage designations, rarity, public engagement favouring preservation, and the planning disruption that demolition would cause, including repealing designations and heritage work delays.

Opponents of the rehabilitation option argued a steel replacement would cost much less, last longer (75 versus 30 years) and improve river flow. One councillor questioned how the environmental assessment scored the options.

Staff said the 30-year figure is a point for reassessment, not a failure date, and that cost estimates include contingency but could change at detailed design. A heritage advisory committee member said peer cities are rehabilitating similar bridges.

On procurement, councillors asked why the City cannot favour local firms. Staff said trade agreements require open, fair processes, and that the new provincial Buy Ontario directive adds compliance work and budget uncertainty.

On energy equity, a delegate urged Council to fully fund the plan. Councillors asked about outreach through trusted community agencies, and staff said budget requests would follow implementation planning.
